rules: Licence text is QUOTED from the publisher, never paraphrased into a permission we wish we had.
robots.txt is obeyed as written. A source whose robots disallows a path is not crawled on that path, whatever the licence says.
A source that did not respond is recorded EXTERNALLY_BLOCKED with its transport error. It is never silently dropped, and never replaced by invented data.

sources.name: Open Food Facts
sources.role: primary — global breadth plus real Saudi/Gulf packaged coverage
sources.access_method: Official bulk CSV export over HTTPS (static.openfoodfacts.org/data/...), downloaded once and streamed. NOT the per-product API.
sources.licence: ODbL 1.0 for the database; Database Contents Licence for individual contents; CC-BY-SA for images.
sources.licence_quote: The Open Food Facts database is available under the Open Database License.
sources.commercial_use_quote: authorize the use and reproduction of the content for all purposes, including commercial use
what_the_terms_actually_permit: Commercial use IS permitted — the terms say so explicitly.

ODbL obligations we therefore take on: (1) ATTRIBUTE Open Food Facts wherever the data is surfaced; (2) SHARE-ALIKE — if we publicly distribute a derived database, it must go out under ODbL; (3) KEEP-OPEN — no DRM that blocks the ODbL rights.

Practical consequence for Qimmah: shipping OFF-derived product data inside the app is a public distribution of a derived database. Attribution must be visible in the UI and the derived shards must carry the ODbL notice. This is an obligation, not an optional nicety.
sources.robots_status: world.openfoodfacts.org/robots.txt disallows /api, /cgi and /facets for User-agent: *. The bulk /data/ export path is NOT disallowed.
sources.robots_consequence: Bulk ingest MUST use the /data/ export. Crawling /api/v2/search for bulk would be against robots and is not done. The app's existing per-scan runtime lookup in src/features/barcode/openFoodFacts.ts is a different thing: one user-initiated request per scan, not crawling.
sources.expected_volume: ~4.2 million product rows in the CSV export; the usable subset (valid GTIN + energy + macros) is far smaller.
sources.saudi_coverage: Real but thin relative to Europe. Measured, not assumed — see the report's source breakdown.

sources.name: USDA FoodData Central — Branded Foods
sources.access_method: Official bulk ZIP download over HTTPS.
sources.licence: US Government work — public domain (17 U.S.C. §105). No attribution legally required, though it is good practice.
what_the_terms_actually_permit: Unrestricted use including commercial, with no share-alike obligation.
Because it carries NO copyleft, it does not contaminate our other data the way ODbL does.
sources.robots_status: fdc.nal.usda.gov/robots.txt is 'User-agent: * / Disallow:' — an empty Disallow, i.e. everything is allowed.
sources.expected_volume: ~2 million branded US food records (194.1 MB compressed JSON).
sources.saudi_coverage: Effectively none — US retail market. Adds global breadth only.
sources.why_not_ingested_in_this_wave: Saudi-first is the product priority and OFF already supplies the Saudi/Gulf rows. Adding ~2M US records would inflate the long tail without serving the Saudi user, and the ingest adapter is the only missing piece — the pipeline is source-agnostic by design. Recorded as a ready extension, not as a blocker.

sources.name: Saudi Food & Drug Authority (SFDA)
sources.access_method: attempted plain HTTPS GET of the site root
sources.evidence: ECONNRESET (connection reset by peer) on https://www.sfda.gov.sa/, https://sfda.gov.sa/ and https://www.sfda.gov.sa/en, with both a pipeline User-Agent and a browser User-Agent.
sources.interpretation: The reset happens at transport level before any HTTP response, so we cannot even read robots.txt or the terms. This is most likely geo/edge filtering of this build machine rather than a deliberate ban on us.
sources.what_we_did_NOT_do: No attempt to bypass the block — no proxy, no VPN, no spoofed origin. A source we cannot reach lawfully and openly stays unused.
sources.next_step_when_unblocked: Read robots.txt and terms FIRST, confirm redistribution rights, then write an adapter. SFDA data may carry reuse conditions that ODbL-derived shards cannot absorb, so it would need its own shard namespace.

sources.name: Saudi Open Data Portal (open.data.gov.sa)
sources.role: wanted — possible official Saudi food/product datasets
sources.access_method: attempted plain HTTPS GET of robots.txt
sources.next_step_when_unblocked: Search the portal catalogue for food/product datasets, read the Saudi Open Data Licence, then decide. Its terms are NOT assumed to be compatible with ODbL redistribution.

sources.name: Manufacturer public nutrition pages (e.g. Almarai)
sources.robots_status: almarai.com/robots.txt is 'User-agent: * / Allow: /' — crawling is not disallowed.
sources.why_not_ingested: robots permitting a crawl is NOT a copyright licence. Nutrition tables published on a corporate site carry no grant of redistribution, and scraping them into a shipped database would be republishing someone else's content without permission. Being technically allowed to fetch a page is not being allowed to redistribute it. This needs an explicit licence or a written permission, which is a founder/legal decision, not an agent decision.
sources.escalation: Owner decision required before any manufacturer data is ingested.

sources.name: Qimmah's own curated datasets
sources.role: the hot set — Saudi/Gulf items that must work offline
sources.licence: Owned by Qimmah. No third-party redistribution constraint.
sources.note: Only PKG-001 carries GTINs, so only PKG-001 enters the barcode-keyed pipeline. The other two are generic foods keyed by name, a different retrieval path, and are left untouched.
